Inspirer, motiver et ouvrir des portes p: Inspiring, motivating and opening doors for racialized youth in Montréal
Des sportifs de haut niveau issus des mi: Elite athletes from minority communities show young people that sport can open the door to other opportunities.
Mehdi Abdesmad (à gauche) ainsi que Zach: Mehdi Abdesmad (left) and Zacharie Belamri (right) open up about their journeys. Photo credit: Nantou Soumahoro
Le sport n’est pas seulement une discipl: Sport is not only a discipline or a competition: it can become a common language, a source of confidence and a tool for social transformation, especially in neighbourhoods where prospects sometimes seem limited. With racialized athletes such as Luguentz Dort and Bennedict Mathurin recently making their mark on the international stage, inspiring a sense of pride in many young people, particularly in Montréal-Nord, this article looks at the impact of a community initiative that opens horizons, sows hope and reminds young people that other paths are possible. How can a meeting, a few words, an example transform a young person's journey?
La jeunesse racisée se heurte encore tro: Racialized youth still run up against a glass ceiling far too often. But a growing number of role models from minority communities, particularly in elite sport, are breaking down barriers and showing that a future full of opportunities is possible. That is what the event Mise au Jeu, organized by Export Support, set out to show young people. Sport can be a starting point rather than an end in itself, and there are many other possibilities to consider.
Malgré la pluie qui s’abat sur Montréal: Despite the rain pouring down on Montréal on this last Friday of June, a good number of families and young people braved the weather and made their way to the <l1>Moroccan cultural centre Dar Al Maghrib </l1>where the event was held. The goal: to learn about volunteering opportunities, but above all to listen to and talk with two professional athletes from the Maghrebi community.
Zacharie Belamri discute en fin de soiré: Zacharie Belamri talks with young people late in the evening. Photo credit: Nantou Soumahoro
À l’intérieur, du thé à la menthe et des: Inside, mint tea and sweets are served while the buzz of conversation fills the room as everyone waits to meet Mehdi Abdesmad, a former NFL player, and Zacharie Belamri, a university soccer player and community activist.
Une fois sur scène, les deux figures par: Once on stage, the two share their journeys, their failures and their victories, and encourage the young people to believe in themselves and to build several plans for the future.
« J’ai perdu mon père au secondaire 5. J: “I lost my father in Secondary 5. I had two choices in life: either I followed the wrong path, or I tried to go down the right path, with school, and then football. And that's what I did,” says Mehdi Abdesmad.
Si les Québécois ayant atteint la NFL so: Few Quebecers have made it to the NFL, and Mehdi Abdesmad had a colourful career despite the obstacles. In his view, sport is a true school of life, one that teaches discipline and pushing past your limits, but above all the ability to reinvent yourself. That is, in fact, exactly what he did.
Mehdi Abdesmad. Crédit photo : Nantou So: Mehdi Abdesmad. Photo credit: Nantou Soumahoro
Formé au Cégep du Vieux-Montréal, il s’e: Trained at Cégep du Vieux-Montréal, he made a name for himself at Boston College before signing with the Tennessee Titans in 2016. After a stint with the Buccaneers in Florida and an early retirement at 26 for health reasons, he went on to work for Ubisoft and is now a real estate broker. “If you're able to learn in your sports career, you'll be able to apply it elsewhere. You'll succeed.”
Une des activités dont il est le plus fi: One of the activities he is proudest of is mentoring young people. “The most important thing for me is to give back to young people what I didn't have: a mentor. Even if I help just one young person, that's what matters,” says the former player, who is of Tunisian origin and smiles constantly.
« Le sport, c’est pas pour la vie », rap: “Sport isn't for life,” Mehdi Abdesmad reminds the audience. He stresses that it's important to be fully committed, but to keep your eyes open to other possibilities. Zacharie Belamri, who is still in university and plays for the Carabins, also insists on the importance of having another path if the first one doesn't work out. Because while sport can be a springboard, it isn't enough to build a lasting future without a parallel plan.
Pour Zacharie Belamri, l’échec n’est pas: For Zacharie Belamri, failure is not an end, but a necessary step toward success. “Once you've failed a lot, you understand that it's something normal,” he says.
Les meilleurs joueurs sont d’ailleurs so: The best players are often those who experienced the most failures early in their careers, he points out. “Nobody succeeds at everything or gets there all at once. The more mistakes you make, the more you learn. That's when you can learn the most.”
Ces mots résonnent auprès de plusieurs j: These words resonate with a number of young people, including Mohamed.
Pour lui, l’événement <em>Mise au Jeu</e: For him, the Mise au Jeu event came at just the right time. Like many young sports enthusiasts, he found himself at a crossroads, torn between his dreams and the doubts that build up over time. “I was going through a period of doubt. I was thinking of quitting.”
En écoutant les témoignages de Mehdi Abd: Listening to the stories of Mehdi Abdesmad and Zacharie Belamri, he says he felt “a second wind.” It was the sincerity of their words, their clear-eyed view of failure and their ability to bounce back that moved him. “Zacharie said it's never too late. You can make it at any age.”
« Ça m’a vraiment motivé. » L’adolescent: “It really motivated me.” The teenager left with Zacharie's phone number so that Zacharie could mentor him, as he also wants to become a soccer player. Reinvigorated by the two athletes' words, he says he is aware that “life isn't a Disney movie.”
Pour les parents, comme Sarah, cette ren: For parents like Sarah, the event was much more than a chance to listen: it was a valuable opportunity to support their children on their personal journeys. She stresses the importance of this kind of event, because it can sometimes be hard for parents to get certain messages across to their kids.
« Ça m'a fait plaisir parce que plusieur: “It made me happy because a lot of their comments, their feedback, their observations. These are things we say, things we repeat. But here, the speakers said them in a way that maybe reaches the kids more, that convinces them more,” she says.
Son fils Hamza, âgé de 13 ans, indique q: Her son Hamza, 13, says the evening gave him an idea of the basics for improving and making progress.
« Je sais que si j'applique ce qu'ils di: “I know that if I apply what they say, there's a chance I'll do better too,” he says. “I really liked it when they talked about techniques for reaching our goals. For example, setting goals little by little so you can progress in the short, medium and long term.”
Inspiré, Hamza envisage déjà de s’engage: Inspired, Hamza is already thinking about getting more involved in sports and community organizations. “I'd like to be like them one day, have everyone listen to me and give advice about what I've been through in my life.”
Un autre jeune, Bediss, nous confie que: Another young person, Bediss, tells us that sport is not only a arena for personal performance but a future career, a way to pass things on: “Me, I'd like to become a football or soccer coach.” Behind that ambition is a desire to share what he has learned, to guide others in turn, to have an impact on the next generations. As if he had already absorbed the evening's fundamental message: receiving is good. Giving back is better.
<l1>Export Support</l1>, coorganisateur: <l1>Export Support</l1>, the event's co-organizer, has been doing groundwork for several years to provide equitable access to education. Its mission rests on three pillars: distributing school supplies at the end of the school year in order to fight waste and ease the financial burden on families.
Tout part d’un simple constat : chaque f: It all starts with a simple observation: every year, in many schools, supplies that are still usable end up in the trash when students empty their lockers. To address this, the organization sets up collection bins in partner schools. Students drop off barely used notebooks, pencils that still work, pencil cases, bags... Everything is sorted, redistributed and recycled to meet the needs of communities in Greater Montréal, Morocco and Haiti.
Ghita et Selma Rehimini, la présidente e: Ghita and Selma Rehimini, the president and the international VP of Export Support. Photo credit: Nantou Soumahoro
Née d’un devoir scolaire qu’a rendu Selm: Born out of a school assignment handed in by Selma Rehimini, the initiative became a reality thanks to the commitment of several students. Their first mission: shipping a container full of supplies to Morocco. “It's an assignment that became reality,” sums up Selma Rehimini, Export Support's international VP. Her advice to young people? Choose a cause you are passionate about, because passion is what allows a small project to become a lasting human adventure.
Sarah a vu ses enfants repartir avec une: Sarah saw her children leave with new motivation and a desire to get more involved, through volunteering or other meaningful activities. “With the résumé exercise, my kids realized they didn't have much to put on it. It pushes them to consider volunteering or other commitments more seriously, so they don't end up with an empty résumé. For me, the goal was achieved with this event,” concludes the mother, visibly delighted.
